title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: On January 27, 2021, the Federal Reserve maintained the federal funds rate target range at 0 to 1/4 percent and continued its asset purchase program at $80 billion per month for Treasury securities and $40 billion per month for agency MBS. The Board unanimously voted to maintain the interest rate on reserve balances at 0.10 percent and approved the primary credit rate at 0.25 percent.
key_points: Federal funds rate target range maintained at 0 to 1/4 percent (0-0.25%)
Monthly agency mortgage-backed securities purchases: $40 billion
Interest rate on required and excess reserves maintained at 0.10 percent
Primary credit rate approved at 0.25 percent
Overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at 0.00 percent with $30 billion per-counterparty daily limit
why_it_matters: This implementation note confirms the Fed's commitment to maintaining an ultra-accommodative monetary policy stance with near-zero rates and $120 billion in monthly asset purchases. The document provides the operational details of how the FOMC's January 2021 policy decision is executed through open market operations.
macro_context: This policy implementation occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic recovery period, maintaining the highly accommodative stance established in March 2020. The $120 billion monthly QE pace and zero lower bound rate policy were designed to support economic recovery and achieve maximum employment while inflation runs above 2 percent.
market_structure_context: The document details operational parameters including the SOMA portfolio management ($80bn Treasuries, $40bn MBS monthly), overnight reverse repurchase facility ($30bn counterparty cap, 0.00% rate), and reinvestment protocols for maturing securities. The repurchase agreement operations support short-term dollar funding market functioning.
